name: Dammam
title: Ship Thickness Measurement Dammam | UTM & Hull Gauging
description: UTM for ships at King Abdulaziz Port, Dammam: hull structure, ballast tank and piping gauging, pre-docking steel estimates and renewal survey support.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Dammam
intro: King Abdulaziz Port in Dammam is the main commercial gateway on Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, and the Aramco loading terminals further up the coast keep crude and gas tankers working the same waters. A superintendent with a ship here usually needs gauging fitted around a short cargo call, a wait at anchorage or a yard booking across the water in Bahrain. We mobilise a team to Dammam from India, measure hull structure, tanks and piping to your scope, and plan the work around the berth window you actually have.

highlights.p: Container and general cargo calls at King Abdulaziz Port leave little idle time, so we agree a selective scope in advance, such as deck, hatch coamings, scrubber overboard lines or a single tank, and work it alongside cargo operations.

Ships trading permanently in the Eastern Province see faster ballast tank coating breakdown, wasted sea-water and fire-main piping and condensation damage in voids. We target those areas first rather than spreading readings evenly across the hull.

highlights.h: Linked to Bahrain and UAE yards
highlights.p: Much Eastern Province tonnage docks at ASRY in Bahrain or at yards in the UAE. Gauging done in Dammam before the ship sails gives the repair yard a measured steel renewal estimate before the vessel arrives.

port.h: King Abdulaziz Port and Shipping in Dammam
p: King Abdulaziz Port Dammam, run by the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani), is the main commercial port on the Kingdom's Gulf coast and serves Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran and the wider Eastern Province. Container traffic, mainline and feeder, makes up much of the activity, with Saudi Global Ports operating terminals in the port. Around the container berths sit general cargo, project cargo, ro-ro and dry bulk berths handling the imports that the region's industry, construction and households depend on. Offshore support vessels, tugs and workboats serving the offshore oil and gas fields also use the port, and the Zamil yard inside it builds and repairs that class of vessel.

How long a ship stays decides what can be gauged. A container ship on a liner schedule may be alongside for little more than its cargo exchange, so work on it is selective and agreed with the master and terminal beforehand. Bulk and general cargo ships discharging into the Eastern Province usually stay longer, and holds become accessible one by one as they are emptied and swept. Ships waiting for a berth lie at the anchorage off the port, which suits pre-purchase and condition gauging reached by launch. North of Dammam, tankers loading at Ras Tanura and Ju'aymah rarely have time for gauging during the loading call itself; that work is better done at anchorage before or after loading, with the operator's agreement, or at a yard.

What sets Dammam apart is how hard the environment works on steel. Summer air temperatures, warm and saline Gulf water and humid nights speed up coating breakdown in ballast tanks, drive condensation in voids, duct keels and cofferdams, and attack sea-water cooling lines, fire mains and air pipes. Ocean-going ships pass through; the feeder, offshore and regional tanker fleets that work from here live in these conditions all year. That creates steady demand for repeat condition gauging between surveys, not only at five-yearly renewals, and for pre-docking gauging before a yard visit across the Gulf of Bahrain or down the coast to the UAE.

facilities.h: Where Gauging Happens in and Around Dammam
p: Most jobs in Dammam are done afloat: alongside at King Abdulaziz Port during cargo operations, or at the outer anchorage while a ship waits for its berth. Afloat work suits deck plating, hatch coamings, exposed piping and any tank the master can have cleaned, ventilated and certified gas-free. For offshore support vessels, tugs and workboats, the Zamil shipbuilding and repair yard inside the port gives full access in dock, including bottom plating, sea chests and the tanks that are hard to reach afloat.

Deep-sea ships from the Eastern Province generally dock elsewhere. ASRY in Bahrain is the established large repair yard closest to Dammam, and the UAE yards take a share of the work. When a ship is heading to one of them, gauging it in Dammam first lets the superintendent send measured wastage, not estimates, with the repair specification, and the yard can order steel before the ship arrives. Outdoor work in the Saudi summer is restricted in the middle of the day, so we schedule deck and shell readings for the early morning and late afternoon and use the hottest hours for work inside tanks.

King Abdulaziz Port general cargo and bulk berths — hold, tank top and hopper gauging as each hold is discharged and swept
Zamil shipbuilding and repair yard, King Abdulaziz Port — in-dock hull, tank and sea-chest gauging on offshore support vessels, tugs and workboats
Dammam anchorage — pre-purchase, on-hire and condition gauging on ships waiting for a berth, reached by launch through the ship's agent
Ras Tanura and Ju'aymah — tanker gauging at anchorage before or after loading, where the terminal operator and the ship's operator agree to it
ASRY, Bahrain — pre-docking estimates and in-dock gauging for Eastern Province ships that dock across the water

context.h: Port State Control, Sulphur Rules and the Eastern Province Fleet
p: Saudi Arabia belongs to the Riyadh MoU, the port state control regime of the GCC states, so ships calling at Dammam are inspected under that regime. Structural wastage, holed air pipes, corroded ventilators and leaking fire-main sections are the kind of finding that a short gauging and inspection visit before arrival can catch while there is still time to repair. The Gulf is not an emission control area: the global sulphur limit of 0.50% under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14, in force since 1 January 2020, is the rule here, and ships with exhaust gas scrubbers can burn high-sulphur fuel. Wash water is acidic and warm, and in Gulf service the overboard pipes, distance pieces and valve bodies downstream of the scrubber are where thinning shows first.

The fleet that calls repeatedly at Dammam is regional: Saudi and Gulf-owned feeder and general cargo ships, offshore support vessels on charter to the oil and gas fields, and tankers lifting from the Aramco terminals up the coast. Long-term charters with energy companies usually carry condition clauses, and tanker charterers and oil-major vetting look closely at structure on ships approaching their third renewal survey. For these owners, thickness gauging in Saudi Arabia is part of keeping a charter as much as passing a survey, which is why trend data from one visit to the next matters.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Dammam
jobs.p: Gauging and ship inspection in Dammam tend to be short, targeted visits rather than full-ship campaigns, because most of the fleet here is either working cargo or about to sail for a yard. The scope is set by what the berth or anchorage time allows and by the decision the owner has to make next: what steel to order, whether to buy the ship, or what to show a charterer.
list: A feeder container ship alongside King Abdulaziz Port: scrubber overboard piping and sea-water cooling lines gauged during a single cargo call, with findings discussed with the chief engineer before departure
A geared bulk carrier discharging into the Eastern Province: hold frames, hopper plating and tank top gauged as each hold is emptied, ahead of its third renewal survey
An offshore support vessel docked at the Zamil yard: bottom plating, sea chests and double-bottom tanks gauged in dock to scope steel renewal before the work package closes
A product tanker at the Dammam anchorage: pre-purchase gauging of deck, cargo tank deckheads and ballast tanks for a buyer's technical team
An LPG carrier due at ASRY: pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks and hull structure in Dammam, so the yard receives a steel estimate before the ship crosses to Bahrain

logistics: Our team flies into King Fahd International Airport, which has direct services from several Indian cities, and travels by road to Dammam or to the landing point for the anchorage. Access to King Abdulaziz Port needs ISPS gate passes, which the ship's agent applies for with each technician's passport and visa details; anchorage work needs a launch, also booked through the agent. Indian technicians need a Saudi business visit visa, so we start the application as soon as the vessel's dates are firm and keep the agent informed. For a planned yard visit, that lead time sits comfortably inside normal drydock planning.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a container ship during a short call at King Abdulaziz Port?
faqs.a: Yes, if the scope is matched to the window. A liner call leaves time for selective work, such as upper deck, hatch coamings, accessible ballast or fuel tank boundaries and scrubber overboard lines, but not for the full gauging a renewal survey needs. Send us the call schedule and the areas of concern, and we plan readings so the team is off the ship before cargo work ends. Larger scopes are better done at anchorage or in dock.

faqs.q: Which areas corrode fastest on ships trading permanently in the Eastern Province?
faqs.a: On ships that stay in the Gulf, the heaviest wastage usually turns up in ballast tanks with failed coatings, especially those next to heated fuel tanks or engine-room bulkheads, in sea-water cooling and fire-main piping, in air pipes and ventilators on deck, and in voids where condensation collects overnight. A gauging plan for a Gulf-based ship should weight those areas, rather than copying the pattern used for an ocean-going ship.

faqs.q: Do you work at Ras Tanura and the other terminals, or only in Dammam port?
faqs.a: Our team goes to wherever the vessel is and the authorities allow access. Aramco terminals such as Ras Tanura run strict access and safety rules, and a tanker's loading time is rarely the moment for gauging. We normally work tankers from this area at anchorage before or after loading, at a yard, or at the next port that gives a longer stay, all arranged through the ship's agent.

faqs.q: How much notice do you need for UTM services in Dammam?
faqs.a: For UTM services in Dammam, the Saudi business visit visa has to be issued and the port passes approved before the team flies. Visa processing is the longest step, so the earlier you confirm the job, the more flexible we can be. For a drydock in Bahrain or the UAE booked months ahead, that is rarely a problem; for a short-notice call, tell us the vessel's dates as soon as they are firm.
